title: Mutual Fund Charges Were Trimmed in April. Who Gave Way?

beats.say: What does a mutual fund company earn on every hundred rupees? At ICICI Prudential, the second largest fund house by mutual fund assets, it is fifty three paise a year, by the company's own measure. It keeps thirty seven as profit, before tax. The rest goes on costs. But in April, the rule on what a fund may charge was trimmed. The company says that had no negative impact on it. So who gave way?
beats.cap: What does a mutual fund company earn on every ₹100? At ICICI Prudential AMC, the second largest fund house by mutual fund assets, it is 53 paise a year, by the company's own measure. It keeps 37 as profit, before tax. The rest goes on costs. But in April, the rule on what a fund may charge was trimmed. The company says that had no negative impact on it. So who gave way?

beats.say: On the first of April, the rules on that charge changed. HDFC A M C's chief executive listed the changes. First, an extra five paise per hundred rupees, which fund houses could charge in place of a fee for leaving early, was taken off. Second, government levies were counted outside the charge. Third, limits on brokerage were revised. So who felt these changes?

beats.say: A moat is whatever keeps rivals away from a business's profit, like water around a fort. Not the price: the regulator limits what a scheme may charge, and the managing director said those expenses keep falling as a fund grows. Nor falling costs.
